I have farmed a long time, and at my age I will keep the plan steady, familiar, and manageable. I will put 7.0 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation and keep 3.2 mu in stevia, because that matches my land, my labor, and the well water I can rely on. For wheat, I will use improved seed and moderate fertilizer, because I want a stable stand through winter and a dependable harvest without pushing costs too hard. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 7.0 mu and keep the operation simple, with no-tillage seeding if conditions allow, because the wheat-maize rotation leaves a short turnaround and I do not want to lose moisture or time. For stevia, I will manage it a little more carefully on the smaller area, with more potassium and a few more sprays, because leaf quality matters and it needs cleaner field management. Overall, I will choose steady yields, lower labor pressure, and reliable irrigation over taking big risks.
